'''Prem Chand Pandey''' is an Indian [[space scientist|space]], and [[Planetary science|planetary scientist]], academic in the fields of satellite [[oceanography]], [[remote sensing]], [[atmospheric science]], the [[Antarctic]] and [[climate change]],<ref>[http://www.ncaor.gov.in/pages/view/391/395-professor-prem-chand-pandey "Professor Prem Chand Pandey's profile at NCAOR web page as founding Director/1st former Director"]. Professor Prem Chand Pandey's profile at NCAOR web page as founding Director/1st former Director</ref> and the founding director of the [[National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research|National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)]].

==Education and career==
Pandey obtained his masters and bachelor's degrees in Electronics and science respectively from [[Allahabad University]]. He completed his [[D.Phil.]] degree from the same university<ref>[http://www.iitkgp.ac.in/fac-profiles/showprofile.php?empcode=2bmVT&depts_name=N2 Faculty page] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124082715/http://iitkgp.ac.in/fac-profiles/showprofile.php?empcode=2bmVT&depts_name=N2 |date=24 November 2010 }}, Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.</ref><ref name="auaa.in">[http://auaa.in/?page_id=31 " Pandey is Proud Past Alumni of Allahabad University"] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120707073335/http://auaa.in/?page_id=31 |date=7 July 2012 }}. Pandey is told AU’s Product in Allahabad University Alumni Association web page.</ref> (on [[microwave]]s) in 1972.<ref>{{cite book |last=Sahoo |first=Dinabandhu|date=2002 |title=Advances in Marine and Antarctic Science |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nEBRPxtp4W0C&q=Prem+Chand+Pandey+allahabad+university&pg=PA449 |publisher=APH Publishing |pages=449 |isbn= 9788176483476}}</ref>

In 1966, Pandey became a lecturer in DAV Degree college, [[Azamgarh]]. From 1968 to 1972 he was [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] Research Fellow at the microwave research laboratory of the Department of Physics, University of Allahabad, and from 1973 to 1977 a research officer at the Central Water and Power Research Station, [[Khadakwasla]]. In 1977 he joined the [[Space Applications Centre]] (SAC)/ [[ISRO]], Ahmedabad and became the founder head of the Oceanic Sciences Division/ Meteorology and Oceanography Group/ Remote Sensing Applications Area (OSD/ MOG/ RESA). He worked for the next twenty years at SAC. In the 1980s he was also a research associate at the [[NASA]] – [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]], [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]], where he worked on the [[Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite]] and [[SEASAT]] programs.<ref>a) [https://ntrs.nasa.gov/search.jsp?No=0&N=4294850820&Ns=HarvestDate%7c1&as=false NASA TECHNICAL REPORTS SERVER Selected Navigations: Author Pandey, P. Allahabad University official web page.</ref> He was Visiting Professor at the Center for Ocean, River, Atmosphere and Land Sciences (CORAL), [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur|IIT Kharagpur (IIT-Kgp)]] from 2005 to 2007 then Emeritus Professor from 2007 to August 2011, playing a key role in the establishment of the CORAL.<ref>a) [http://www.financialexpress.com/printer/news/189104/  Changing global weather pattern causing concern] Dr PC Pandey of Kharagpur-based Indian Institute of Technology has study"Tele-connection between melting of Antartica Sea ice and the frequency of El Nino and Southern Occillation phenomena (ENSO)". b) Numerical Simulation of Bay of Bengal Circulation Features from Ocean General Circulation Model P C Pandey Author From IIT Kharagpur</ref> He joined the faculty of School of Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences, [[Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar|IIT Bhubaneswar]] as a Professor with effect from 1 September 2011.<ref>[http://www.iitbbs.ac.in/pdf/Newsletter_Rhythm_4-9-2011.pdf "Prof. P C Pandey Joins IITBBS"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120422040701/http://www.iitbbs.ac.in/pdf/Newsletter_Rhythm_4-9-2011.pdf |date=22 April 2012 }}.  (PDF) A doctorate in Physics (Microwaves) from Allahabad University, he is credited with the initiation of the satellite borne microwave remote sensing of Ocean Atmosphere and Cryosphere research in India. Professor Pandey was the Founder Director of National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research, Goa from 1997 to 2005. He has spent a major part of his career at Space Application Centre (ISRO), Ahmedabad, and has worked for about five years at the NASA’s world famous Jet Propulsion Laboratory, USA. Professor Pandey has carried out extensive research in the areas of satellite oceanography, atmospheric science, climate change and polar science................He was also a member of the delegation led by Hon’ble Kapil Sibal to Antarctic, the first ever ministerial delegation to visit Antarctica. Professor Pandey has represented India in various International symposia related to Polar Science and Logistics such as Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR), Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting (ATCM) etc. Professor Pandey is the recipient of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award (1989), Professor Vikram Sarabhai Award and Gold Medal, Om Prakash Bhasin Award and [[Vigyan Gaurav Award]] of U.P. Council of Science and Technology as well as the NASA award:IIT Bhubaneswar web page says.</ref><ref>[http://www.ias.ac.in/php/fell_all.php3?alpha=P " Professor Pandey at present at School of Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences, Indian Institute of Technology, Samantapuri, Bhubaneswar-751 013"]. According to the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] Pandey is Faculty of IIT Bhubaneswar.</ref><ref>[http://www.iitbbs.ac.in/portfolio.php?id=d09bf41544a3365a46c9077ebb5e35c3 "Faculty Profile of Prof. Prem Chand Pandey"]. School of Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences, IIT Bhubaneswar, Faculty profile of Professor Pandey</ref><ref>[http://www.iitbbs.ac.in/faculty/iit_1338424939.pdf "Brief resume of Professor Pandey"]. (PDF) This brief resume describes that he is Faculty at IITBBS and good information about him can be found here</ref> where also he played key role in establishment of the School of Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences, [[Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar|IIT Bhubaneswar]] and after a satisfactory development of this school, Dr. Pandey returned to [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur|IIT Kharagpur (IIT-Kgp)]] and worked as Emeritus Professor since 20 November 2017 as to 25 November 2020.<ref>[http://www.iitkgp.ac.in/department/CL/former-faculties "Pandey is listed as Former Faculty Member of CORAL, IIT Kharagpur 2005-2011 and 2017 to 2020"]. Pandey is listed as Former Faculty Member of CORAL, IIT Kharagpur.</ref> Currently he is working as adjunct professor at Department of Earth Sciences,  [[IIT Gandhinagar]] since 1 January 2021.<ref>[https://iitgn.ac.in/faculty/earths/fac-pcpandey "IIT Gandhinagar faculty page of Professor Pandey"]. IIT Gandhinagar faculty page of Professor Pandey</ref>

* Member, ICSU/WMO committee for [[International Polar Year]] (IPY) framework documents preparation.<ref>[http://www.icsu.org/2_resourcecentre/Resource.php4?rub=8&id=121 "International Polar Year 2007–2008"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113174349/http://www.icsu.org/2_resourcecentre/Resource.php4?rub=8&id=121 |date=13 November 2008 }}. Prem Chand Pandey was Member, ICSU/WMO committee for International Polar Year (IPY) framework documents preparation</ref>
* President (sectional); Environmental Science Section, [[Indian Science Congress Association]], 2006–7.<ref>[http://sciencecongress.nic.in/html/pdf/everyman_Oct_Nov_06.pdf President (sectional); Environmental Science Section] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619085223/http://www.sciencecongress.nic.in/html/pdf/everyman_Oct_Nov_06.pdf |date=19 June 2009 }}. (PDF) EVERYMAN’S SCIENCE,
 science congress web page say that Dr. Pandey was sectional President</ref> 
* Also remained member of Executive Council of the Indian Geophysical Union (1991–1993).<ref>[http://www.igu.in/members.htm#1991-93 " P C Pandey is member"]. Pandey is member of the executive Council</ref>

==Works==

Pandey has published more than 134 research papers,<ref>[http://www.geographyandyou.com/sagaa/ "Science and Geopolitics of Arctic and Antarctic: The Organising Committee of SaGAA 2011"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711084709/http://www.geographyandyou.com/sagaa/ |date=11 July 2011 }}. Conference at India International Centre web page stated that Dr. Pandey has published 134 research papers</ref> 7 books, 9 reports and 4 Atlases, and has guided 11 PhDs. He has also edited the journals ''Marine Geodesy'',<ref>[http://www.tandf.co.uk/journals/journal.asp?issn=0149-0419&linktype=5 Associate Editors]. Marine Geodesy...</ref> ''Indian Journal of Polar Science'', 2008 and the Remote Sensing section in ''Mausam'', the quarterly research journal of [[India Meteorological Department]].<ref>[http://www.imd.gov.in/mausam/subedit.htm Subject Editors – Mausam] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090513000232/http://www.imd.gov.in/mausam/subedit.htm |date=13 May 2009 }} [[India Meteorological Department]].</ref> He has been a member of the editorial board of the ''Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing''<ref>[https://www.springer.com/earth+sciences/journal/12524?detailsPage=editorialBoard Editorial board: Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing] springer.com, Earth Sciences.</ref> ''Indian Journal of Radio & Space Physics'' (IJRSP),<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.niscair.res.in/sciencecommunication/ResearchJournals/rejour/ijrsp/ijrsp0.asp | title=Csir-Niscair }}</ref> ''Indian Journal of Marine Science'', India (1995–2000), ''Vayu Mandal'', Bulletin of Indian Meteorological Society, (1995–1996), ''Proceedings of Indian Academics'' (Physical Sciences) and the ''Journal of Indian Society of Remote Sensing'' (2006).
